title: Data policies (DLP) for Copilot Studio agents
summary: Hold: the page says Microsoft has not explained how existing virtual-connector settings should carry over, but Microsoft now documents configuring replacement agent settings to match them. The control paths and commands are supported; the scope explanation should also acknowledge that ACP-only mode stops enforcing classic data policies.

claims.claim: A Power Platform data policy groups connectors and decides which connectors an app, flow or agent can use together.
claims.quote: A core component of Power Apps, Power Automate, and Microsoft Copilot Studio is the use of connectors to enumerate, populate, push, and pull data. Power Platform admin center data policies allow administrators to control access to these connectors

claims.claim: Learn also calls these data loss prevention (DLP) policies.
claims.quote: The policies that define how data can be shared are referred to as data loss prevention (DLP) policies.

claims.claim: Connectors are classified in Business, Non-Business or Blocked groups.
claims.quote: The three data groups are the Business data group, the Non-Business data group, and the Blocked data group.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters; summary
claims.claim: Data policies govern Copilot Studio agents in every environment covered by the policy's scope.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.
claims.fix: Add this qualification to the scope explanation and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/advanced-connector-policies: 'In ACP-only mode, classic data policies are ignored for the affected scope, even if they remain configured; do not rely on them there for connector, endpoint or virtual-connector restrictions.' The cited agent guide gives the general scope, while the ACP guide documents this exception.

claims.claim: Connectors in different data groups cannot share data.
claims.quote: The key point is that connectors in the same group can share data in Microsoft Power Platform, whereas connectors in different groups can't share data.

claims.claim: An app or flow cannot use both SharePoint in Business and Gmail in Non-Business.
claims.quote: if you place SharePoint and Salesforce connectors in the Business group and you place Gmail in the Non-Business group, makers can't create an app or flow that uses both the SharePoint and Gmail connectors.

claims.claim: A connector in Blocked cannot be used where the policy applies.
claims.quote: Blocked connectors can't be used where this policy is applied.

claims.claim: Data policy enforcement has been in effect for all tenants since early 2025.
claims.quote: Since early 2025, data policy enforcement is in effect for all tenants, as announced in the message center alert MC973179: Copilot Studio - Upcoming updates to data loss prevention enforcement.

claims.claim: Agents cannot be exempted from data policy enforcement since March 2025.
claims.quote: Since March 2025, agents can't be exempted from data policy enforcement. It's no longer possible to exempt agents with a PowerShell command.

claims.claim: Virtual connectors are not based on a REST API.
claims.quote: Virtual connectors are connectors that appear in data policies for administrators to control, but they're not based on a RESTful API.

claims.claim: The described Agent status experience is preview documentation for standard-harness agents.
claims.quote:
This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: Add all environments configures tenant-wide policy scope.
claims.quote: Add all environments: Adds all the environments in your entire tenant. This policy automatically applies to any new environment created in the tenant.

claims.claim: Tenant-level data policies can include or exclude selected environments.
claims.quote: Tenant-level policies can be defined to include or exclude specific environments.

claims.claim: Learn says connectors introduced after 2019, including unauthenticated chat and Direct Line, are likely to be in default Non-business.
claims.quote: Connectors introduced after 2019, such as Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio or Direct Line channels in Copilot Studio, are likely to be part of the default "Non-business" group.

claims.claim: Learn says many organisations automatically block the Non-business group.
claims.quote: In many organizations, connectors in the "Non-business" group are automatically blocked.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that default blocking of new connectors can cause outages affecting Direct Line or unauthenticated website agents.
claims.quote: Misaligned configurations, such as data policies blocking new connectors by default, could result in production outages. For example, essential features like Direct Line or unauthenticated agent deployments on websites might be unexpectedly blocked.

claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform data policies DLP licensing separate license charge data policy. Opened wp-data-loss-prevention, prevent-data-loss, dlp-connector-classification and admin-data-loss-prevention; these specify roles or connector licensing, not a separate data-policy licence.

claims.claim: The documented tenant-level policy procedure requires the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level policies require Environment Admin permissions where there is no Dataverse database.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions. For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: Environment-level policies require System Administrator instead if the environment has a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: New connectors normally enter the policy's designated default group.
claims.quote: You must designate one data group as the default group to automatically classify any new connectors added to Microsoft Power Platform after you create your policy.

claims.claim: Non-Business is initially the default group.
claims.quote: Initially, the Non-Business group is the default group for new connectors and all services.

claims.claim: New nonblockable connectors enter Non-Business even with Blocked as the default group.
claims.quote: If Microsoft adds any new connectors that can't be blocked and you set the default group for the data policy as Blocked, these connectors are automatically marked as Non-Business instead of Blocked.

claims.claim: A Blocked default group blocks newly introduced blockable connectors.
claims.quote: If the new connector setting is Blocked, any new connectors that are blockable are mapped to Blocked, as expected.

users of the agent see a DataLossPreventionViolation error when trying to interact with it.

claims.where: Open questions: virtual connector settings carrying over
claims.claim: Microsoft does not say how existing data-policy settings carry over when Copilot Studio virtual connectors move to dedicated governance rules.
claims.quote:
Configure the dedicated agent settings for the same scope so that they match your current Copilot Studio virtual connector settings:
Agent access channels for publishing channels.
Authentication for agents for agent authentication.
Skills in Copilot Studio for skills.
claims.fix: Replace this open-question bullet with: 'Microsoft's ACP migration guidance tells administrators to configure dedicated agent settings for channels, authentication and skills to match their current Copilot Studio virtual connector settings.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/advanced-connector-policies#migrate-from-data-policies-to-acp. Do not assert automatic migration: the documented instruction is to configure matching settings.
